goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the current project rooted at the cwd where pi was opened (treat any nested .git as a separate project boundary — do not walk into parent or sibling projects). Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

Scope: the current project rooted at the cwd where pi was opened (treat any nested .git as a separate project boundary — do not walk into parent or sibling projects). Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix

Lead: Task and goal proposals validate before side effects and disclose milestone commands — fixed in 5ae4e281.
Lead: Loop refinements stage spec changes atomically before mutating live state — fixed in bd117be1.
tests: Focused repair, list, revision, and transactional-refinement suites passed.

Lead: Vision fallback arguments are shell-quoted and executed against a sentinel fake CLI — fixed in ee50dd3.
Lead: Published docs and schema tests now match runtime contracts — fixed in b1e4a818.
tests: Settings, vision, schema, release-contract, security, and display focused suites passed.
npm audit: 0 vulnerabilities.

auditHistory.report:
I'll start by understanding the project structure and the audit artifacts.

I checked the 12 files for affected regions and all tests pass—40 out of 40. The earlier 48-failure run was misleading because I included behavioral-orchestrator and revision-bound-audit test suites that spawn detached auditors, which timeout and cause cascading failures due to module-state coupling. Now I'm verifying those two files individually to confirm they behave correctly on their own.

All verification complete. Now I'll write the audit report with the evidence section.

---

# Audit Report — completion of "fresh project audit pass" goal

## Objective
Run one fresh audit pass with ≥3 parallel scouts, append new findings (FIX/DECIDE) to `.pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md`, fix every new FIX finding with a commit + checked box, raise every DECIDE finding to the user and record DECIDED/DEFERRED, and leave the project in a known state.

## What I verified (skeptical, evidence-first)

**1. Fresh parallel scout fan-out (≥3 in one message).**
`audit/FRESH-AUDIT-2026-09-23/launch-record.json` (committed in 2f18fa49) records workflow `876cf269-f827-4de0-b166-e92a0175bea8` with **four** `scout` children dispatched in a single `runs.all` workflow (timestamps 1790189233–1790189301, all in the same dispatch; reports at `lifecycle-recovery.md`, `queue-auditor.md`, `commands-ui.md`, `tests-docs-packaging.md`). ≥3 parallel: satisfied. Two scouts exited with code 1 due to a pre-existing staged-files condition in the host session (staged files: `.pi-glla/active.jsonl` etc., pre-dating the audit) — their child reports themselves passed all content criteria and produced findings; the rejection is a host hygiene artifact, not missing survey work. All four reports exist and were cross-referenced into findings.

**2. Findings appended, classified, no re-reporting.**
`.pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md` contains `## Fresh project audit — 2026-09-23 (v0.38.97)` (line 562) plus `## Priority field follow-up — 2026-09-23` (line 555). Every new finding is `- [x] FIX: SEVERITY: … — fixed in <commit>`; the new section's findings cite commits that I confirmed all exist on `main` (`git cat-file -e` on all 43 cited SHAs: every one OK, no MISSING). Dedup note present ("candidates independently re-read against the current tree; duplicates and disproved claims were excluded"). Append-only file structure preserved (findings.md is 145 KB, the new sections are appended at the end of history at lines 555–608).

**3. Every new FIX has a fix commit + checked box.**
I sampled all cited commit SHAs — all 43 exist in the repository on main (spot-checked full list including `c3e22da9, e3442cb6, a6ccc9ad, 44c95861, 681ec05a, b59f44d8, 26df745e, 79b12b01, 36ad1450, ed9472ab, bd117be1, 50db98b5, 36a754b3, 26673820, ee50dd3, 8a98e3c9, 5ae4e281, b1e4a818`). Each box in the 2026-09-23 sections is `[x]` with a named commit. Honesty law holds: no unchecked FIX boxes remain in the new sections.

**4. DECIDE findings.**
`grep -n "\[?\]" .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md` → **0** open DECIDE lines. Line 599 states plainly: "No new DECIDE finding remained: the auditor-bash confidentiality choice was already resolved in the append-only history." The auditor-bash confidentiality decision had indeed been resolved earlier (line 12: fixed in 5f1e9c8f with `--no-approve`, read-only allowlist, five-minute timeout — i.e., the "confidentiality boundary" question was decided in the prior audit cycle and the fix landed). So the "report states plainly that none were found" alternative of the contract is met. No `ask_user_question` gate was needed for a new DECIDE this pass.

**5. Verification claims cross-checked, not taken on trust.**
- Reran the two load-timeout files exactly as claimed: `bun test tests/glla-stale-context.test.ts tests/compaction-survival.test.ts --parallel=1 --max-concurrency=1 --timeout=60000` → **9 pass, 0 fail** (I got 9.68s vs their 10.34s — consistent).
- Reran the 12 specific affected regression files together → **40 pass / 0 fail** in 7.86s.
- `npm run check` (tsc --noEmit) → exit 0, clean.
- Reran `tests/revision-bound-audit.test.ts` alone → 18/18 pass; `tests/behavioral-orchestrator.test.ts` alone → 151/151 pass. (When I first batched all 13 files, some orchestrator/revision tests timed out — I confirmed this is a known test-isolation/load artifact of process-wide module state in those behavioral suites, not a product regression: each file passes 0-fail in isolation, and the affected test logic (branch ownership fence, one-shot directive consumption, repair revision bump) matches the committed source fixes. The executor's VERIFICATION.md itself documents the 2 full-suite load timeouts as load-sensitive, and its bounded rerun reproduces clean.)
- `git status --short`: only `M .pi-glla/active.jsonl` (live runtime ledger, expected noise). No stray staged source changes left in the tree.

**6. Quality of the fixes (not just paperwork).**
Spot-reads confirm the fixes are substantive, not placeholders:
- `extensions/goal-loop.ts` branch-ownership fence (c3e22da9 +63/−16) before every mutating Git boundary, with a durable park path (no destructive reset/checkout after failure) — matches the "Stop destructive finish after failed status/add/commit/reset/checkout" task.
- `extensions/goal-recovery.ts` (26df745e) makes stale-auditor persistence transactional and has the caller check the result; the "stopped claiming safe while restart still reads `auditing`" false-claim is closed by the checked-state append (7cd35443 adds 55-line regression).
- `extensions/loops/goal-tools.ts` revision bump on repair contract change (ed9472ab +24/−3) closes the stale-same-revision-approval hole.
- Vision shell-quoting (ee50dd3), subagent name traversal block (8a98e3c9), detached-auditor minimal-env (492ba8b1) all have named regression tests in-tree.
- Docs/schema alignment (b1e4a818) replaces the stale hand-written schema test with a schema-driven one, as task 14.4 required.

Every one of the 17 goal-task groups maps to a real commit + regression I could trace. The "independent fresh reviewer PASS" claim and the 2558-pass canonical gate are consistent with my targeted reruns; I did not re-run the 2558-test full suite (bounded), but the affected-file reruns all pass, typecheck is clean, and the two load-timeout files pass in the documented bounded rerun.

## Judgment
The objective is genuinely satisfied: a real fresh multi-scout audit was run in parallel; findings were appended append-only with no re-reports; every new FIX has a real, inspectable commit on the current branch with a checked box and a regression; no open DECIDE remained and the report states that plainly (with the earlier confidentiality decision traceable in history); and the verification contract is met with evidence that I independently reproduced. No missing requirement, no weak verification, no scope drift.

auditHistory.report:
I'll start by understanding the project structure and the audit artifacts.

I checked the 12 files for affected regions and all tests pass—40 out of 40. The earlier 48-failure run was misleading because I included behavioral-orchestrator and revision-bound-audit test suites that spawn detached auditors, which timeout and cause cascading failures due to module-state coupling. Now I'm verifying those two files individually to confirm they behave correctly on their own.

All verification complete. Now I'll write the audit report with the evidence section.

---

# Audit Report — completion of "fresh project audit pass" goal

## Objective
Run one fresh audit pass with ≥3 parallel scouts, append new findings (FIX/DECIDE) to `.pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md`, fix every new FIX finding with a commit + checked box, raise every DECIDE finding to the user and record DECIDED/DEFERRED, and leave the project in a known state.

## What I verified (skeptical, evidence-first)

**1. Fresh parallel scout fan-out (≥3 in one message).**
`audit/FRESH-AUDIT-2026-09-23/launch-record.json` (committed in 2f18fa49) records workflow `876cf269-f827-4de0-b166-e92a0175bea8` with **four** `scout` children dispatched in a single `runs.all` workflow (timestamps 1790189233–1790189301, all in the same dispatch; reports at `lifecycle-recovery.md`, `queue-auditor.md`, `commands-ui.md`, `tests-docs-packaging.md`). ≥3 parallel: satisfied. Two scouts exited with code 1 due to a pre-existing staged-files condition in the host session (staged files: `.pi-glla/active.jsonl` etc., pre-dating the audit) — their child reports themselves passed all content criteria and produced findings; the rejection is a host hygiene artifact, not missing survey work. All four reports exist and were cross-referenced into findings.

**2. Findings appended, classified, no re-reporting.**
`.pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md` contains `## Fresh project audit — 2026-09-23 (v0.38.97)` (line 562) plus `## Priority field follow-up — 2026-09-23` (line 555). Every new finding is `- [x] FIX: SEVERITY: … — fixed in <commit>`; the new section's findings cite commits that I confirmed all exist on `main` (`git cat-file -e` on all 43 cited SHAs: every one OK, no MISSING). Dedup note present ("candidates independently re-read against the current tree; duplicates and disproved claims were excluded"). Append-only file structure preserved (findings.md is 145 KB, the new sections are appended at the end of history at lines 555–608).

**3. Every new FIX has a fix commit + checked box.**
I sampled all cited commit SHAs — all 43 exist in the repository on main (spot-checked full list including `c3e22da9, e3442cb6, a6ccc9ad, 44c95861, 681ec05a, b59f44d8, 26df745e, 79b12b01, 36ad1450, ed9472ab, bd117be1, 50db98b5, 36a754b3, 26673820, ee50dd3, 8a98e3c9, 5ae4e281, b1e4a818`). Each box in the 2026-09-23 sections is `[x]` with a named commit. Honesty law holds: no unchecked FIX boxes remain in the new sections.

**4. DECIDE findings.**
`grep -n "\[?\]" .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md` → **0** open DECIDE lines. Line 599 states plainly: "No new DECIDE finding remained: the auditor-bash confidentiality choice was already resolved in the append-only history." The auditor-bash confidentiality decision had indeed been resolved earlier (line 12: fixed in 5f1e9c8f with `--no-approve`, read-only allowlist, five-minute timeout — i.e., the "confidentiality boundary" question was decided in the prior audit cycle and the fix landed). So the "report states plainly that none were found" alternative of the contract is met. No `ask_user_question` gate was needed for a new DECIDE this pass.

**5. Verification claims cross-checked, not taken on trust.**
- Reran the two load-timeout files exactly as claimed: `bun test tests/glla-stale-context.test.ts tests/compaction-survival.test.ts --parallel=1 --max-concurrency=1 --timeout=60000` → **9 pass, 0 fail** (I got 9.68s vs their 10.34s — consistent).
- Reran the 12 specific affected regression files together → **40 pass / 0 fail** in 7.86s.
- `npm run check` (tsc --noEmit) → exit 0, clean.
- Reran `tests/revision-bound-audit.test.ts` alone → 18/18 pass; `tests/behavioral-orchestrator.test.ts` alone → 151/151 pass. (When I first batched all 13 files, some orchestrator/revision tests timed out — I confirmed this is a known test-isolation/load artifact of process-wide module state in those behavioral suites, not a product regression: each file passes 0-fail in isolation, and the affected test logic (branch ownership fence, one-shot directive consumption, repair revision bump) matches the committed source fixes. The executor's VERIFICATION.md itself documents the 2 full-suite load timeouts as load-sensitive, and its bounded rerun reproduces clean.)
- `git status --short`: only `M .pi-glla/active.jsonl` (live runtime ledger, expected noise). No stray staged source changes left in the tree.

**6. Quality of the fixes (not just paperwork).**
Spot-reads confirm the fixes are substantive, not placeholders:
- `extensions/goal-loop.ts` branch-ownership fence (c3e22da9 +63/−16) before every mutating Git boundary, with a durable park path (no destructive reset/checkout after failure) — matches the "Stop destructive finish after failed status/add/commit/reset/checkout" task.
- `extensions/goal-recovery.ts` (26df745e) makes stale-auditor persistence transactional and has the caller check the result; the "stopped claiming safe while restart still reads `auditing`" false-claim is closed by the checked-state append (7cd35443 adds 55-line regression).
- `extensions/loops/goal-tools.ts` revision bump on repair contract change (ed9472ab +24/−3) closes the stale-same-revision-approval hole.
- Vision shell-quoting (ee50dd3), subagent name traversal block (8a98e3c9), detached-auditor minimal-env (492ba8b1) all have named regression tests in-tree.
- Docs/schema alignment (b1e4a818) replaces the stale hand-written schema test with a schema-driven one, as task 14.4 required.

Every one of the 17 goal-task groups maps to a real commit + regression I could trace. The "independent fresh reviewer PASS" claim and the 2558-pass canonical gate are consistent with my targeted reruns; I did not re-run the 2558-test full suite (bounded), but the affected-file reruns all pass, typecheck is clean, and the two load-timeout files pass in the documented bounded rerun.

## Judgment
The objective is genuinely satisfied: a real fresh multi-scout audit was run in parallel; findings were appended append-only with no re-reports; every new FIX has a real, inspectable commit on the current branch with a checked box and a regression; no open DECIDE remained and the report states that plainly (with the earlier confidentiality decision traceable in history); and the verification contract is met with evidence that I independently reproduced. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: Fixed the GLLA-owned default compaction projection so oversized preparation input is hard-bounded before Pi's summarizer, including arbitrary message counts, tool groups, multimodal blocks, GLLA payloads, and previous-summary input. · Changed: `extensions/compaction-input.ts` enforces a configurable hard total bound, preserves complete tool-call/tool-result groups including interleaved records, bounds `previousSummary` while leaving Pi authoritative, and reports omission telemetry; hook comments/tests cover all default paths; the live report distinguishes the 200k context cap from the separate summarizer output ceiling. · Evidence: real Pi 0.87.1/OpenRouter run PASS on a copied historical session with automatic `overflow`, projection `189094 → 13201`, successful summary and continuation, checksum match; report at `audit/COMPACTION-DEFAULT-PROJECTION-LIVE-PROOF.md`. · Tests: `npm test` PASS (2294 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail); typecheck PASS; focused tests PASS (24); report non-empty; diff check PASS. · Unresolved: provider runs remain intermittently capable of redacted `summarization_length`; the immediately preceding current-code run passed and is recorded, while a later run after report-only edits failed. No tag or publication performed. · Next: rerun the exact live verifier during a stable provider window if a post-report PASS is required.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: Fixed the GLLA-owned default compaction projection so oversized preparation input is hard-bounded before Pi's summarizer, including arbitrary message counts, tool groups, multimodal blocks, GLLA payloads, and previous-summary input. · Changed: `extensions/compaction-input.ts` enforces a configurable hard total bound, preserves complete tool-call/tool-result groups including interleaved records, bounds `previousSummary` while leaving Pi authoritative, and reports omission telemetry; hook comments/tests cover all default paths; the live report distinguishes the 200k context cap from the separate summarizer output ceiling. · Evidence: real Pi 0.87.1/OpenRouter run PASS on a copied historical session with automatic `overflow`, projection `189094 → 13201`, successful summary and continuation, checksum match; report at `audit/COMPACTION-DEFAULT-PROJECTION-LIVE-PROOF.md`. · Tests: `npm test` PASS (2294 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail); typecheck PASS; focused tests PASS (24); report non-empty; diff check PASS. · Unresolved: provider runs remain intermittently capable of redacted `summarization_length`; the immediately preceding current-code run passed and is recorded, while a later run after report-only edits failed. No tag or publication performed. · Next: rerun the exact live verifier during a stable provider window if a post-report PASS is required.

completionRecap.objective: Finish the durable GLLA-owned fix begun in session 01a0d307 for Pi default auto-compaction failures at 99–100% context. Make every default `session_before_compact` invocation robustly project oversized, tool-heavy, multimodal, and GLLA-bearing preparation input into a bounded summarizer payload while preserving message order and roles, assistant/thinking/text content, tool-call/tool-result pairing, previous-summary semantics, split-turn metadata, `fileOps`, `firstKeptEntryId`, and durable `.pi-glla` goal/list recovery state. Pi remains authoritative for cut-point selection, summarization, persistence, retries, and final compaction result; the solution must use the public hook rather than modifying Pi core, changing provider/model/reserve/thinking settings, or relying on parallel/recursive retries. Diagnose and close any remaining gap exposed by the reported historical failures, add regression and integration coverage for all supported preparation shapes and repeated hook invocation, and prove the fixed code in a newly started Pi process against a copied historical session with a real provider-backed default compaction that completes without a token-cap/incomplete-summary error and permits a successful continuation afterward. Keep the work local and release-ready but do not tag or publish externally; do not mix in the deferred `extensions/drafting-interview.ts` work.
